items.title: Listening on purpose or hearing by accident

states.label: The doing marked
states.note: The belonging word *a* marks the boy as a doer listening on purpose.

states.label: The hearing happens to him
states.note: The belonging word *o* makes the hearing something that happened to him.

items.caption: The same verb takes both belonging words with different readings. Hearing and seeing are the pair the chapter shows doing this.

items.title: What closes the choice?

data.question: Which word forces *o* in this le-phrase?

prompts.sm: le lē pese o le teine
prompts.why: A negated event did not take place. The not-word forces *o*.

prompts.sm: le fia pese o le teine
prompts.why: Wanting to sing is not singing. The want-word forces *o*.

prompts.sm: le pese soʻo o le tama
prompts.why: The often-word makes this a habit rather than one event that happened, and forces *o*.

items.intro: Find the word inside the event that settles the belonging word before the doer test can run.

items.title: Two participants, either order

states.label: Doer first
states.sm: le fafaga e le tina o le pepe
states.en: the mother's feeding of the baby
states.note: The mother keeps the agent marker because the thing fed is named with *o*.

states.label: Thing fed first
states.sm: le fafaga o le pepe e le tina
states.en: the mother's feeding of the baby
states.note: The same two marked phrases stand in the other order.

items.caption: Both printed orders are ordinary Samoan. Moving the two phrases does not exchange their markers or their jobs.
